timeline.change: Wagoneer launched (November 1962) with the 230 OHC Tornado six; two- and four-door wagons and a panel delivery; IFS optional on 4x4s
AMC 327 V8 and 232 six arrive; IFS dropped from 4WD models; standard safety package with dual brakes
Super Wagoneer: 270 hp 327, TH400, tilt wheel, A/C; about 3,989 built by 1969
Buick 350 Dauntless V8 (to 1971); two-door Wagoneer dropped at year-end; solid axles and leaf springs only from 1969
Quadra-Trac full-time 4WD introduced, three years after AMC bought Kaiser Jeep
Two-door Cherokee launched (base and S); 401 V8 offered; front discs standard on the Wagoneer
Boxed frame rails and stronger crossmembers; wide-track Cherokee Chief arrives
Wagoneer Limited arrives mid-year; last year of the 401
'Pig nose' grille, square headlights, aluminum bumpers; last year of the TH400 and the Borg-Warner Quadra-Trac
TorqueFlite 727 automatic; NP219 'Quadra-Trac' and part-time NP208; Wagoneer output falls to 10,481 after the fuel crisis
Selec-Trac standard on the Wagoneer; Pioneer package; last year of the SJ Cherokee. For 1984 the Wagoneer Limited becomes the Grand Wagoneer

identify.intro: Three Jeeps called themselves Cherokee or Wagoneer in the 1980s, the Chief package is easy to fake with stickers, and the drivetrain changed almost every year, so check the VIN, the axles and the transfer case.

items.head: SJ vs XJ
items.body: The SJ is body-on-frame on a 108.7 in wheelbase with six-lug wheels (from 1974). The 1984-on Cherokee and the 1984–90 Wagoneer Limited are compact unibody XJs.

items.head: Real wide-track Chief
items.body: Chiefs from 1976 have wider axles and larger fender flares, and were never built as four-doors. Golden Eagles add denim seats, gold-painted steel wheels and a big gold hood eagle.

items.head: VIN, 1981–83
items.body: Character 4 is the engine (C = 258 six, N = 360 V8); 5 is the transmission and transfer case; 6–7 are the body (15 = Wagoneer, 16/17 = two-door Cherokee, 18 = four-door Cherokee); 10 is the year (B = 1981, C = 1982, D = 1983); 11 is the plant (T = Toledo, B = Brampton). The VIN is also stamped on a tag on the upper-left firewall.

items.head: Early VINs
items.body: Pre-1981 VINs use an older, shorter format. Wikipedia lists the first-year 1974 Cherokees as Model 16 (base) and Model 17 (S).

items.head: Transfer case
items.body: 1974–79 automatics with a single floor lever have the Borg-Warner Quadra-Trac; 1974–79 manuals have a Dana 20. From 1980 look for a tag reading NP208, NP219 or NP229; Selec-Trac trucks have a 2WD/4WD switch.

capability.note: wide-track Chief at the top of the range
1983 Wagoneer, 258 six, automatic and Selec-Trac, per Wikipedia; V8s are far thirstier

values.intro: SJ Wagoneers and Cherokees sell for less than the woodgrain Grand Wagoneer. Low-mileage originals and V8 restomods bring the big money, and the two-door Cherokee carries a premium over the Wagoneer.
values.note: Based on 31 Bring a Trailer sales of SJ Wagoneers and Cherokees from October 2025 to October 2026 (median about $19,000, middle half $11,600–28,000). Top originals: a 1975 Cherokee S at $80,000 and a 29,000-mile 1983 Wagoneer Limited at $51,000. A Viper-powered 1979 Cherokee Chief restomod made $315,000. Hagerty puts a good-condition 1976 Cherokee Chief at about $14,100.
